summary: Highbury Airport is a small regional airfield serving the remote community of Highbury in Far North Queensland, Australia. Located in the Gulf Country region, it primarily supports general aviation and serves as an important access point for the surrounding pastoral and Indigenous communities. The airport features a single unsealed runway typical of remote Australian outback airstrips.
faqs:
Q: What type of aircraft can use Highbury Airport?
A: The airport primarily accommodates small general aviation aircraft, including single-engine planes commonly used for charter and private flights in remote Queensland.

Q: Are there scheduled commercial flights to Highbury?
A: No scheduled commercial services operate from this small airfield; flights are typically charter-based or private operations.

Q: What facilities are available at the airport?
A: As a small rural airstrip, Highbury Airport offers minimal infrastructure with no terminal building, so passengers should arrange ground transport in advance.

Q: When is the best time to fly into Highbury?
A: The dry season (May to October) generally offers the most reliable flying conditions, as the wet season can bring heavy rains and reduced visibility.
transport_tips: Ground transport must be pre-arranged as there are no taxi or shuttle services available at this remote airfield. Visitors typically rely on private vehicles or hosts from the local community for pickup. The nearest significant town with rental car services is approximately a long drive away, so plan logistics before arrival.
local_tip: Always carry extra water, sun protection, and a satellite phone or PLB when flying into Highbury, as the surrounding Gulf Country can be extremely isolated with limited mobile reception and harsh conditions, especially during the wet season.
